question: {"question": "What is TIMEOUT_CYCLES and what happens on timeout?", "proposed_default": "100000000 cycles (1 s); a part-way packet is dropped silently with no counter change."}

reply.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000 cycles, not 100000000 as proposed. The specification does not say what happens on timeout, so the proposed silent drop with no counter change cannot be confirmed from the spec.

question: {"question": "Is the class code for 'not new' one class, or are repeat and out of order separate?", "proposed_default": "One class with one counter (six counters in total)."}

reply.answer: Not one class. Repeat (RESULT 5, counter 0x14) and stale (RESULT 6, counter 0x15) are separate classes with separate counters. The spec has seven counters in total, not six. The protocol counter 0x16 covers both bad type and bad length.
reply.quote: Counters 0x10 good, 0x11 bad check, 0x12 short, 0x13 long, 0x14 repeat, 0x15 stale, 0x16 protocol (type and length), 16-bit wrapping.

question: {"question": "Are the class codes as proposed (0 none, 1 too long, 2 too short, 3 bad check, 4 unknown, 5 not new, 6 good)?", "proposed_default": "Codes 0 to 6 as listed, numbered in rule order."}

reply.answer: No. The specification lists the class codes as 0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length. The proposed codes (1 too long, 2 too short, 3 bad check, 4 unknown, 5 not new, 6 good) do not match, so the proposed default is rejected.
reply.quote: RESULT: offset 0x01, RO, reset 0: class of the last packet: 0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length

question: {"question": "Is a packet with a zero-byte body or only the end flag byte counted as too short?", "proposed_default": "Yes, any packet under 4 bytes is too short."}

reply.answer: Yes. A packet that ends before 4 bytes is classed SHORT (3), so a packet holding only the end-flag byte (one byte) is too short. The spec does not separately address a zero-byte body, but any such packet is also under 4 bytes.
reply.quote: 'SHORT (3): ends before 4 + LEN + 4 bytes, or before 4 bytes.'

question: {"question": "Do the type, sequence and payload registers keep the last good packet or the last packet of any class?", "proposed_default": "Last good packet only."}

reply.answer: Partly. TYPE, SEQ and PAY0 hold the last good packet only, so the proposed default holds for them. PAY1 is not settled: the behaviour text says it is zeroed by every new packet, which conflicts with keeping the last good packet's value. The specification does not say which applies to PAY1 after a refused packet, so the default cannot be confirmed for PAY1.
reply.quote: bits: type of the last good packet; bits: sequence number of the last good packet; bits: first two payload bytes of the last good packet, big-endian, zero filled; PAY1 5 (next four, big-endian; zero fill and zeroed by every new packet)
